threat_description: Detect when PowerShell executes with obfuscated parameters, downloads files from the internet, and writes to suspicious locations.

sigma.rule:
title: Detect when PowerShell executes with obfuscated parameters, downloads files
id: 4e966c89-bc7c-4460-a85f-c2f758ae0b56
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: powershell
detection:
  powershell_execution:
    Image|endswith: \\powershell.exe
    CommandLine|contains:
    - powershell
    - ps.exe
  network_activity:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
    - DownloadFile
    - WebClient
    - wget
    - curl
    - http
    - ftp
  obfuscation:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
    - EncodeCommand
    - -NoP
    - Replace
    - SubString
    - base64
  file_write:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
    - .exe
    - .dll
    - .vbs
    - .ps1
    - .bat
    - .cmd
  condition: powershell_execution and network_activity
tags:
- detection.threat_hunting
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059
- attack.t1105
references:
- https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma
- https://attack.mitre.org

snort.rule: alert tcp any any -> any any (msg:"Detect when PowerShell executes with obf [T1059]"; content:"GET"; http_method; content:"http"; http_uri; content:"encoded"; nocase; flow:to_server,established; sid:5027448; rev:1;)

yara.rule:
rule Detect_when_PowerShell_executes
{
  meta:
    author = "Security Team"
    date = "2025-12-15"
    description = "Detect when PowerShell executes with obfuscated pa"
    mitre_techniques = "T1059, T1105"
  strings:
    $ps1 = "powershell" nocase
    $ps2 = "cmd.exe" nocase
    $web1 = "http" nocase
    $web2 = "DownloadFile" nocase
  condition:
    any of them
}
